Surah al-Muddaththir (74) is Meccan, and its verses number fifty-six.

﴿O you who are wrapped up (al-Muddaththir)﴾: the Prophet (ﷺ). Its original form is al-mutadaththir, and the taa' was assimilated into the daal, meaning: the one wrapped in his garments at the time the Revelation descended upon him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 74, verse 2:

﴿Arise and warn.﴾ Warn the people of Makkah of the Fire if they do not believe.
﴿And your Lord, glorify⁠﴾ magnify Him above the association of the polytheists (with Him).
﴿And your garments, purify﴾ from impurity, or shorten them, contrary to the Arabs who trailed their garments out of arrogance, so that impurity would often reach them.
﴿And the abomination﴾: the Prophet (ﷺ) explained it as idols. ﴿So forsake﴾, i.e., persist in forsaking it.

﴿And do not confer favor, seeking more﴾. It is read in the nominative (bi-al-raf', as a ḥāl, a circumstantial qualifier). The meaning is: do not give anything while seeking to receive more than it in return. This is specific to the Prophet (ﷺ), because he was commanded to adopt the most beautiful character and the noblest manners.
﴿And for your Lord, be patient﴾ in carrying out the commands and avoiding the prohibitions.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 74, verse 8:

﴿So when the trumpet is sounded﴾ — it is blown into the Ṣūr, which is the horn, the second blast (al-nafkha al-thāniya).

**[Then that]**, i.e., the time of the blast, **﴿that day﴾** is a substitute (*badal*, a grammatical apposition) for what precedes it, which is the subject (*mubtada'*, the grammatical topic). It is indeclinable (*mabni*) because it is attached to a word that is *غَيْر مُتَمَكِّن* (ghayr mutamakkin, a noun that does not take the full range of case endings). The predicate of the subject is **﴿a difficult day﴾**. The element governing *إذا* (idha, "when/at the time that") is what the sentence implies: "the matter became severe."
﴿upon the disbelievers, not easy﴾. This indicates that it is easy for the believers in their hardship.

﴿Leave me﴾ "utrukni" (leave me alone), ﴿and whom I created﴾ is in apposition (ʿaṭf) to the object of the verb, meaning "me," or it is an object of accompaniment (mafʿūl maʿahu), ﴿alone﴾ "waḥīdan" is a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) of "man" (whom), or of its omitted pronoun in "khalaqt" (I created), meaning "solitary, without family or wealth."
